chunks: But when he reached it, a voice called out: 'Blessed is He who is in the fire and all around it. Praised be God, the Lord of all the worlds.'

key_terms.بُورِکَ: Blessed is He / May He be blessed
key_terms.سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ: Praised be God / Glory to God

ai.seo_question: What does the phrase 'Blessed is He who is in the fire' mean in Surah An-Naml?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse marks the transition from Musa's (AS) earthly journey to his spiritual reception of the Tawrat, emphasizing that divine blessing (Barakah) permeates both the fire and the surrounding space, symbolizing God's omnipresence. The phrase 'Subhan Allah Rabb al-Alamin' serves as a cosmic declaration of God's transcendence, linking the specific location of Tuwa to the broader theological concept of the 'Sacred Valley' as a locus of revelation. This moment underscores the Shia understanding of the Prophet's unique status as the recipient of divine speech, setting a precedent for the Imams as inheritors of this spiritual authority.
